correctness.rationale: For residue Jordan type (2^a,1^(d-2a)), square-zero lift count equals q^((d-a)^2+a^2) by anticommutant-to-commutant isomorphism and module-Hom dimensions. Gaussian image/kernel/isomorphism choices yield exactly |GL_d(k)|/[P_aP_(d-2a)] after multiplication. Euler product follows by coefficient identities. Explicit convergent tail bounds prove the fixed-q O_q(1/d) uniform-rank theorem. Reproducible independent enumeration and kernel ranks confirm exact small cases for split and ramified rings, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The identified prime-power matrix polynomial enumeration assumes a square-free residue polynomial (Cheong–Liang–Strand, Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and Remark 1.2), while the present t-squared equation is repeated-root and not covered. Danchev–García–Gómez Lozano prove existence of square-zero lifts, not fiber sizes. A prior dimension-two count does not imply uniform higher-dimensional strata or total-variation asymptotics. Comparison against related studies and statement-level searches identified no equivalent count; older broad Hall/jet formula risk remains.

value.rationale: Cheong–Liang–Strand expressly exclude polynomial equations whose residue polynomial is not square-free; the naturally occurring square-zero equation is the first repeated-root case. The result classifies every residue-rank stratum in all dimensions d>=3 for both chain-ring types with a complete normalized generating function; its asymptotically uniform residue-rank law is structurally unexpected and neither a special-case table nor an unmotivated coefficient calculation.
